coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: P24
names: P24 -- waterfront lawn (Bayfront Park approach, south of 499 Illinois St)
record.summary: A triangular waterfront lawn with a curved path south of 499 Illinois Street, labelled P24 on OCII's December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map; it visually resembles Bayfront Park's own style and may be a continuation of it (an observation from satellite imagery, with no document cited), and its outline was traced by hand by Pier & Point as the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes, not taken from a surveyed parcel boundary. OCII's September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P24' among the parcels the Port of San Francisco 'will manage' (not among the 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being built by then. Name and specific operator not confirmed by any source found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- landscaped open land (lawn, curved path, scattered trees) as seen in Esri satellite imagery (an imagery observation; no document cited), outlined as the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes and cut by hand by Pier & Point at a point where the shape forks, rather than at a surveyed parcel boundary. Name and operator not confirmed by any source found; a hedged observation from imagery (no source cited) that it visually resembles Bayfront Park's own style and may be a continuation of it.
notes.digitized_from: Outlined as the open ground left between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes around the 499 Illinois St / Bayfront Park area (one piece of 19,181.78 sqm before cutting). Pier & Point split that piece in three at its two natural narrow points (lat 37.7658 and 37.76665) and then cut it by hand the same way as P26: the wide, single 'head' was kept and the thin, branching 'horns' were dropped. Not taken from a surveyed parcel.

open_questions: The April 2019 SocketSite article names the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park' -- not to be confused with Mariposa Park, OCII's own official P26 per its current open-space page (a separate, larger playground park at Mariposa and Owens streets; see the open questions on Pier & Point's record for P26, the landscaped wedge at the 16th/3rd/Owens St interchange, for a related P26 label conflict). Not reconciled here, only noted so the two 'Mariposa'-named places aren't conflated.

No source names this specific lawn or gives its own construction date beyond the April 2019 under-construction report; the Sept 2023 OCII document only establishes it existed and was already Port-managed by that date, which is an upper bound, not a build date.

Not confirmed whether this lawn was built as part of Bayfront Park's own 2024 construction (which it visually resembles and adjoins) or earlier, as part of 409/499 Illinois Street's 2008 completion (whose developer's own project page describes 'nearly an acre of waterfront outdoor space' at that building, per SKS Partners' project page) -- no source ties this specific parcel's completion to either project, so no more specific date is asserted.

Whether OCII's own current numbering scheme still uses 'P24' for exactly this footprint was not independently confirmed -- OCII's current public Mission Bay South open-space page (sfocii.org/projects/mission-bay-south/open-space) does not list a P24 at all among the parcels it names (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P26).

As of 2026-09-29, no source read says Mariposa Bayfront Park (P23/P24) was under construction in April 2019, only that its completion was expected by the end of 2019, and no post-2019 source read confirms it was finished; the Sept 2023 OCII deck ('will manage', not 'when built') is the only completion evidence. OCII's November 2024 CAC map, said to show P23 and P24 as completed park, was not checked.
